title: Rural Home Loans: Scheduled Principal Pending on an Automatic Debit
content:
Payment operations answers on Rural Home Loans scheduled principal that is still to post from an imminent automatic debit, when a balance is tested against the escrow waiver limit.

## Rule

Scheduled principal still to post is taken off the tested balance as follows: when the loan pays by automatic debit, its next payment falls due within 15 days and that payment is not the final scheduled payment, the principal share of that next payment is taken off, the share being the monthly principal-and-interest payment less one month's interest on the principal balance at the note rate, rounded to the cent; when the loan pays by automatic debit, its next payment falls due within 15 days and that payment is the final scheduled payment, the whole principal balance is taken off, since the final payment carries all principal outstanding; otherwise nothing is taken off. The amount is taken off the tested balance before the limit amount is subtracted.

## Questions and answers

**What does "within 15 days" mean?** The next due date on the loan record is no more than 15 calendar days after today.

**How is one month's interest figured here?** The principal balance on the loan record multiplied by the note rate, divided by 100 and divided by 12, rounded to the cent.

**When is the next payment the final scheduled payment?** When the next due date is the maturity date on the loan record.

**What if the loan does not pay by automatic debit?** Nothing is taken off, however close the due date.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, automatic debit enrolled)

| Days from today to the next due date | Final payment | Taken off |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | no | the principal share of the next payment |
| 16 | no | nothing |
| 10 | yes | the whole principal balance |

*Worked figure:* principal 240100.00 at 6.125 percent gives one month's interest of 1225.51; with a monthly principal-and-interest payment of 1531.20 the principal share is 305.69.
